long_biography.plain_text:
Historical documents assembled by Spanish financier José María Castañé form a collection at Harvard’s Houghton Library. Over 25 years, he gathered manuscripts, photographs and books recording the upheavals of the twentieth century. His interest in history reached back to childhood memories of relatives discussing the events of the Second World War.

Castañé established a foundation to preserve his holdings and donated part of the archive to Harvard to broaden its use in research and teaching. The material ranges from Truman’s corrected announcement of Germany’s surrender and Churchill’s appointment cards to soldiers’ letters and diaries, preserving personal experiences alongside the decisions of political leaders.
